summary.text: Wendy Peer is the Democratic candidate for the Arkansas House of Representatives, District 50, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where she faces incumbent Republican Zack Gramlich.
An educator, she said in a Ballotpedia survey that she has spent 20 years in radio and television and 15 years in public education.

paragraphs.text: Wendy Peer graduated from Parkwood High School, earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Arkansas in 2010 and a graduate degree from Arkansas Tech University in 2018, according to Ballotpedia.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she has lived in Fort Smith for more than 37 years after moving there from Missouri, and has four children, four grandchildren and two great-grandchildren.

Peer said her campaign has three main messages, beginning with fully funding public schools, holding all taxpayer-funded schools to the same academic and financial standards, and opposing voucher programs.
She also listed economic security for families, including affordable child care, SNAP and WIC, and school meals, and defending Medicaid and Medicare and supporting rural hospitals.
She listed the Arkansas Education Association, Vote Common Good 2026, Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate Distinction and Pro Arkansas Women among her endorsers.
